content.comment_body: When I run the online test (refer to the attached picture), the actual states of the blocks aren’t shown. Analog input values for AI1 and AI2 appear, but the rest of the program doesn’t seem active. The program works as expected in real usage, so I’m unsure what’s wrong. I’m using [product_name] with firmware [version_no]. Are there any known issues? Thank you. P.S. My other three [product_name] systems at home work fine in Online Test, so it’s only device number 3 with this issue.

Screenshots like these make it difficult to determine whether network or physical inputs are receiving a high signal. Could you clarify what leads you to believe the program isn’t functioning correctly?
Could you upload your program files as a ZIP? Also, what firmware do your other three [product_name] devices have?

I understand your challenge—without the complete overview, it’s hard to diagnose. I’ve marked some sections in the updated picture for clarity. If block B040 ('NOT' function) in the lower left corner receives a low input, its output should be high. Similarly, the 'High' block in the center should output high but still shows a blue line instead of red. These cases can’t both be correct. The issue seems limited to 'Online test', since the actual program operates fine. For example, when I turn on the bathroom light (input I9 is high), the fan (output Q12) activates with the set delay, as expected. But Online Test doesn’t reflect this. If there are any known issues with Online Test in this situation, let me know. Devices 1, 2, and 4 work well in Online Test. Here are the firmware versions for reference: Device 1: [version_no], Device 2: [version_no], Device 3: [version_no], Device 4: [version_no].
As requested, here is my home automation project:

You are right, there’s an issue. I don’t have a [product_name] with firmware [version_no], only versions [version_no], [version_no], and [version_no]. When I upload your program to my [product_name] with [version_no], Online Test works fine. [IMAGE]
Try updating your firmware. Information about the firmware update for [product_name] regarding security vulnerability CVE-2020-7593: you can update from [version_no] to [version_no].

Thanks for your help. I updated the firmware for devices 1, 2, and 3; device 4 already had the needed version. Online Test now works perfectly. The [product_name] manual says to format the SD card to FAT32 (default) but my PC defaults to FAT, which is actually FAT16 and can be easily missed. This prevents the firmware upgrade. I also encountered an issue with device 2: after inserting the SD card, the holder ejected itself and I couldn’t remove the holder. I had to open the housing and carefully push the SD card out with a fine screwdriver. In the end, it worked and I can continue adding functions to my home automation system.

Glad to hear it. Yes, the SD card must be formatted with FAT32, and storage shouldn’t exceed 32 GB. With older [product_name] models, the card slot can be finicky, but the newer [product_name] model improves on this significantly.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encountered a discrepancy between actual operations and the Online Test display for a particular [product_name] device. The program executed correctly in reality, but Online Test failed to show the real-time status of blocks, causing confusion and raising reliability concerns about the tool. Firmware version mismatches were pinpointed as the cause, demonstrating the importance of keeping firmware updated for dependable diagnostics. Issues with SD card formatting and insertion also complicated firmware upgrades, affecting usability.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect Online Test to reliably display the live status of all program blocks regardless of firmware version. They also want firmware upgrades and troubleshooting to be simple, without encountering SD card formatting or device compatibility issues.
